podcast.title: Financial Struggles and Limited Promotion (1988)
podcast.body: In 1988, Sub Pop was described as a "tiny struggling local record label" that was "perpetually broke," lacking the necessary money or influence to effectively promote its releases. This limited the reach of bands like Mudhoney, despite their pioneering sound. "Subpop was perpetually broke, so it didn't have the money or cloud to promote their releases."

podcast.title: Nirvana's First Single Release (1988)
podcast.body: Sub Pop Records was the label responsible for issuing Nirvana's very first single in October 1988, a release that is now identifiable by unique dead wax inscriptions. "issued on subpop records in October of 1988"

podcast.title: Post-1988 Grunge Publications
podcast.body: From 1988 onwards, Sub Pop released many publications that are almost officially recognized as grunge. Nirvana's first album, *Bleach*, was released on Sub Pop in 1989. "a partir de 1988 la evolución del granch es mucho más fácil porque ya en su pop tenemos muchas publicaciones ya que las conseguimos casi oficialmente granch y en el 89 se aliaba el lich el primer disco en Irvana también en su pop."

podcast.title: Financial State in 1989
podcast.body: In 1989, when Nirvana recorded their debut album "Bleach," Sub Pop Records out of Seattle was described as "perpetually broke." "The band was a completely non-entity at the time, recording for the perpetually broke subpop records out of Seattle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Singles Club (1989)
podcast.body: In 1989, Sub Pop Records ran a "Singles Club" that mailed subscribers a random 7-inch single every month. The very first release through this club was Nirvana's "Bleach" single, mailed out on November 1, 1989, with 1,000 copies hand-numbered in red pen on the white center label, becoming highly valuable collectibles. "This was a club where the label mailed you a seven inch single every month, a random seven inch single."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Codifying Seattle Sound
podcast.body: Sub Pop released Soundgarden's first two EPs, "Screaming Life" and "FOP," which were instrumental in codifying the distinct "Seattle sound." "Subpop released Soundgarden's first two EPs, Screaming Life and Thop, which helped codify the Seattle sound."

podcast.title: Defining Grunge
podcast.body: After signing Green River, Sub Pop co-founder Bruce Pavitt described their second EP in a label catalog as "ultra-lucy Grunge that destroyed the morals of a generation," a quote that significantly contributed to the adoption and stickiness of the "grunge" genre name. "Bruce Pavitt described their second EP in a label catalog as, quote, ultra-lucy Grunge that destroyed the morals of a generation. Unquote, the genre name stuck."

podcast.title: Early Grunge Catalyst
podcast.body: Sub Pop was a small, "perpetually broke" independent record label that played a key role in the early grunge scene by releasing songs from local bands, such as Mudhoney's "Touch Me I'm Sick" in early 1988. "Then along came a small, perpetually broke independent record label called Subpop, which really songs from local bands like this."

podcast.title: Foundational for Grunge
podcast.body: Sub Pop was the principal independent record label in Seattle responsible for almost all the initial developments of grunge music. Many early grunge bands originated here before moving to larger labels. "la principal era supo casi todo el inicio del granch, nacen el supo para luego saltar a Geffen."

podcast.title: Founding and Early Signings
podcast.body: Co-founded by Bruce Pavitt, Sub Pop Records is a legendary Seattle label that signed Soundgarden to their inaugural recording contract. Soundgarden's 1987 debut single, "Hunted Down," notably served as the label's telephone hold music for several years. "Subpop wound up signing Soundgarden to their first recording contract."

podcast.title: Halifax-Seattle Connection
podcast.body: Sub Pop signed Sloan for their first album, "Smeared," contributing to the perception between late 1991 and 1993 that Halifax was becoming the "new Seattle" due to its burgeoning music scene. This signing linked Canadian indie rock with a prominent American alternative label. "largely because of this band who ended up being signed to Subpop for their first album."

podcast.title: Home for Underground Grunge
podcast.body: As the grunge movement became more mainstream and bands like Nirvana moved to Geffen, the more underground and pure side of grunge continued to reside at Sub Pop. "la parte más andegranada un pura se quedaría en su pop."

podcast.title: Influence on Mint Records
podcast.body: Sub Pop's mission to give a voice to up-and-coming acts served as a direct model and inspiration for Mint Records when it was founded in 1991. "Their whole goal was very much like what we saw with Subpop. They needed to give a voice to the up and coming acts in the lower BC mainland."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Interest in Canadian Talent (1990s)
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, following the success of Nirvana, Sub Pop Records showed interest in signing Canadian bands. This reflected a broader industry "rush to sign Canadian bands" during the era of the Canadian rock revolution, indicating a recognition of the burgeoning talent. "The subpop. Yeah. I remember the subpop came up to Toronto."

podcast.title: Seattle-based Indie Label
podcast.body: Sub Pop is an indie label from Seattle, identified as one of the more important labels in the American Pacific Northwest that released records by bands like Mecca Normal. It was well-known for signing grunge bands and also supported other indie acts. "and Subpop from Seattle."
